html:
The Ethiopia to Djibouti railway was a metre gauge line built by a French company from Djibouti to Addis Ababa between 1897 and 1917, about 780 kilometres long.

Menelik II granted the concession to gain an outlet to the sea that Italy and Britain did not control. The line reached Dire Dawa in 1902, a town created by the railway, and Addis Ababa in 1917.

For most of the 20th century it carried the bulk of Ethiopia's imports and exports, including coffee, and made Djibouti Ethiopia's port. It declined from the 1990s and was replaced in 2016 by the new electric Addis Ababa to Djibouti railway built by Chinese firms.
sum: The Ethiopia to Djibouti railway was a metre gauge line built by a French company from Djibouti to Addis Ababa between 1897 and 1917, about 780 kilometres long.
